description: What a developer machine needs for the harness and the official skills: the tools with the minimum and preferred version of each and where that minimum comes from, the per-repository tools, the official skills and agent plugins, and the agents that install plugins. check-tools.ps1 reports the machine against this list and derives its proposals from it. assertedIn/assertedText are relative to the setup-project skill: tests/Test-Repository.ps1 fails when the quoted text is no longer in that file.
maintenance: Changing a version in skills/setup-project/templates/docs/agents/toolchain.md means updating the matching entry here in the same commit. minimumSource is documented (an official skill states it; documented quotes where) or harness-policy (a stable, non-obsolete release); a tool with neither has no minimum.

assertions.guidance: Windows PowerShell 5.1 runs the harness scripts; pac and PCF tooling are tested against PowerShell 7.
One branch per unit of work needs git. Any version works.

Builds and tests plugins and Custom APIs. The SDK on the machine is independent of the framework the plugins target. The minimum is harness policy: a stable, non-obsolete release. canvas-apps, an optional plugin, needs the .NET 10 SDK.

Tests and lints web resources and PCF controls, and runs the official skills' hooks and MCP servers. The minimum is harness policy, above every documented one: the pinned ESLint 10.12.0 accepts Node ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24, and Vitest 5.0.1 accepts ^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0. Together: Node 22.13 or later on the 22 line, or 24, or 26 and later. Vitest rejects Node 20 and the odd-numbered 23 and 25.

assertions.assertedText: | Power Platform CLI (`pac`), the Windows installer | above 2.10.0 | latest |
assertions.guidance: Generates PCF projects and early-bound classes, and reads the environment. The minimum is documented by model-apps, and it is exclusive: 2.10.0 itself does not meet it. Install the Windows installer, not the .NET global tool: it keeps older versions side by side, updates with pac install latest and switches with pac use. It also needs an authentication profile that reaches DEV, which dv-connect creates.
Runs the Dataverse skills' scripts (scripts/auth.py) and SDK. dv-connect installs it and its packages; this check only reports it.
Required by the model-apps and power-automate skills. They state no minimum version.

assertions.assertedText: | GitHub CLI (`gh`) | The repository is on GitHub |
assertions.guidance: Pull requests and repository operations for a repository on GitHub.

assertions.assertedText: | `az` `azure-devops` extension | The repository is on Azure DevOps |
assertions.guidance: az repos and az devops for a repository on Azure DevOps. Detected with az extension list: az devops itself offers to install the extension interactively, so this check never calls it.

recommended.guidance: Manual checks of PCF controls and web resources in their DEV forms. It loads no tool schemas or accessibility trees into the agent's context.

skillPackages.guidance: Mandatory. Installed once per user with npx skills, which every Agent Skills agent reads from ~/.agents/skills. A copy installed as an agent plugin is accepted with a warning; a second copy next to the npx one is a duplicate.

agents.label: Claude Code
agents.note: A plugin update applies after Claude Code restarts.

agents.label: Codex CLI
agents.note: Not exercised by the harness yet. Plugin hooks run only once the user trusts them in /hooks, and the Codex IDE extension has no plugin support.

agents.label: VS Code
agents.note: Not exercised by the harness yet. Whether VS Code agent mode loads the plugins Copilot CLI installed is unverified.
